mbm-0618.clue: I paint the pavement after a shower.
mbm-0618.quote: The puddle outside the laundromat held the whole blue awning. Then a wheel went through it. I had just enough paint on my brush to keep one blue stripe before the street stole it back.

mbm-0619.clue: I keep a drawer full of first sentences.
mbm-0619.quote: A stuck drawer left me with exactly two slips of paper to start my story. One featured a judge, the other a missing sandwich. I've never written anything so quickly.

mbm-0620.clue: I bow to the empty mat.
mbm-0620.quote: At my first karate class I mistook the opening bow for an introduction and told everyone my name. The instructor bowed back and told me hers. Now I greet every new student first.

mbm-0621.clue: I stitch by the color of the sky.
mbm-0621.quote: My weather quilt gets a strip of whatever color I see at breakfast. After six gray mornings the sun broke through. I used a yellow so loud my neighbors could probably hear it.

mbm-0622.clue: I swim to the sound of the drain.
mbm-0622.quote: The old pool has a gurgle at the shallow end. When I practiced backstroke as a kid I thought a frog lived there. I still say good morning before I push off.

mbm-0623.clue: I borrowed a book from a plum tree.
mbm-0623.quote: Somebody built a tiny lending shelf around the trunk. I read my find right there in the shade. A ripe plum fell into my lap at chapter six, so I stayed for seven.

mbm-0624.clue: I like a trick with a stubborn audience.
mbm-0624.quote: I made a green marble vanish for my little sister. She found it in my shoe, where I absolutely hadn't put it. My assistant the cat has since been retired.

mbm-0625.clue: I play the hole behind the whale.
mbm-0625.quote: The big blue whale hides the cup, so I listen for the ball. Last visit I heard two clicks. The kid on the other side had accidentally putted mine back to me.

mbm-0626.clue: I paint one pear every Friday.
mbm-0626.quote: Same table, same saucer, different pear. The bruised one was so purple I painted a second picture before cutting it. Nobody in my house gets to eat fruit without sitting for me anymore.

mbm-0627.clue: I run the long side of the square.
mbm-0627.quote: The florist wheels out his buckets right as I pass. One morning he was late and I went round again to see the tulips. That's my most colorful extra lap.

mbm-0628.clue: I stay seated for the reel change.
mbm-0628.quote: Our neighborhood cinema invited me into the booth. I saw the light pass through one frame held still in the projectionist's fingers. Onscreen it had been a whole train coming home.

mbm-0629.clue: I brought the smallest chess clock.
mbm-0629.quote: Mine winds up and ticks like a cricket. A little boy at our park table spent his whole first game looking under the board. I let him wind the clock for the rematch.

mbm-0630.clue: I sunbathe by the yellow wall.
mbm-0630.quote: The neighbor's canary and I get the same half hour of courtyard sunshine. I stretch out, he sings. When the shade reaches my toes we both go indoors for lunch.

mbm-0631.clue: I saw the matinee from both ends.
mbm-0631.quote: I helped an usher carry a torn seat cushion out between shows. He let me watch the second screening from the balcony. Same movie, but the actor seemed to look right up at me.

mbm-0632.clue: I measure a kilometer in bakeries.
mbm-0632.quote: The first smells like butter, the second like sesame, the third like the rolls I take home. I can run my breakfast loop with my watch buried in the laundry.

mbm-0633.clue: I wrote a program for one bad button.
mbm-0633.quote: My old keyboard typed two spaces whenever I hit the bar. I wrote a tiny typing game where a double space makes the frog leap. Now everybody fights over the broken keyboard.

mbm-0634.clue: I like the moment after I land.
mbm-0634.quote: I pick a blade of grass and slip it into the pocket with my jump log. My first one dried almost white. The whole sky from that morning fits in that little pocket now.

mbm-0635.quote: The team picture in the café window lost its goalie to a tear. I photographed our neighbor posing in exactly that space in the reflection. The owner taped my print beside the original.

mbm-0636.clue: I make the props for anime night.
mbm-0636.quote: Our club screened a cartoon about an airborne bakery. I made a cardboard propeller for the snack tray. We ran out of buns before the plane on screen ever left the ground.

mbm-0637.clue: I run with a folded map in my glove.
mbm-0637.quote: I planned a route that traced a fish across town. I missed a turn and gave it a very long fin. My training partner says that's the part that looks most like me.

mbm-0638.clue: I hike with an empty mint tin.
mbm-0638.quote: At the pass I open it. Inside the lid is the pencil sketch I made on my first climb there. The mountain is much steeper on paper. So was I at fourteen.

mbm-0639.clue: I watch the late show in star pajamas.
mbm-0639.quote: The TV's sleep timer cuts off ten minutes before the mystery ends. My roommate and I make up our own culprit over breakfast. Once we both accused the dog, independently.

mbm-0640.clue: I put an ear on both sides of my cup.
mbm-0640.quote: My father drinks tea with his left hand, my mother with her right. Their shared camping mug got two handles. Dad says the second one is for passing it over.

mbm-0641.clue: I listen for a stone to sing.
mbm-0641.quote: Our curling stone hummed over the fresh pebble one night. Even the skip put his broom down to listen. I threw it too far because I wanted another second of that sound.

mbm-0642.clue: I know my shoes by the odd eyelet.
mbm-0642.quote: Someone repaired my bowling shoe with a brass eyelet. Every other one is silver. When our league mixed up its shoes under the bench, mine winked at me from the very back.
